solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Singer with personal hygiene problem is our nearest relative

parts.note: Bono is the lead singer of the Irish band U2
BO is body odour, the classic hygiene complaint

explanation.surface: A rock star with a body odour problem turns out to be our closest kin.
explanation.definitionFit: This ape species shares the chimpanzee's place as the primate genetically closest to humans.

clue.text: Newton tucked into cheese and pickle

indicators.note: one thing tucked into another sits inside it, so the scientist's letter goes inside the cheese

parts.note: Brie is a soft French cheese
N is the symbol for the newton, the unit of force

explanation.surface: Someone named Newton tucks into a ploughman's lunch of cheese and pickle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tucked into' reads as eating; here it means placed inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Salty water used for preserving food is what vegetables are pickled in, so a pickling liquid.

clue.text: Malodorous moose in Barking

indicators.note: barking means mad, so the letters of the two words go crazy into a new order

explanation.surface: A smelly moose turns up in Barking, a district of east London.
explanation.walkthrough: Barking is an east London place name; here it is the slang sense, crazy.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe something with an offensive, unpleasant smell.

clue.text: Vegetable husks cut by old American dame

indicators.note: something cut by another is split open with the other piece inserted into the gap

parts.note: bran is the husks of cereal grain
DBE, Dame Commander of the Order of the British Empire, is the honour that makes a woman a dame

explanation.surface: An elderly American woman cuts the husks off something in the kitchen.
explanation.walkthrough: A British damehood is the honour DBE.
explanation.definitionFit: This large flat bean, grown in many gardens, is a common vegetable.

clue.text: Ghostly figure accompanied by entertaining artist

indicators.note: to entertain a guest is to hold them within, so one piece holds the other

parts.note: with means accompanied by
RA is a Royal Academician, a member of the Royal Academy of Arts

explanation.surface: A spooky figure appears alongside a painter who amuses the company.
explanation.definitionFit: A wraith is an apparition, a spectre or ghost.

clue.text: Lift shafts, so to speak

indicators.note: so to speak marks words that are to be heard spoken rather than read

parts.note: shafts of light are rays

explanation.surface: A remark about lift shafts in a building, with a modest 'so to speak'.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lift shafts' reads as one phrase, the shafts of an elevator; split it.
explanation.definitionFit: To lift something is to raise it.

clue.text: Bad months after one's exam

indicators.note: one piece placed after the other puts the shorter one second

parts.note: one is, said in the first person, becomes I'm
m is the usual abbreviation for month or months
an oral is a spoken exam

explanation.surface: Months spent waiting after an exam can feel bad.
explanation.definitionFit: Morally wrong or wicked conduct can be described as bad.

clue.text: Minions in hospital infuriate boy

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hospital on road signs
to anger is to infuriate
a son is a boy

explanation.surface: Underlings in a hospital make a young patient furious.
explanation.definitionFit: Hangers-on are followers and sycophants, like minions attached to someone powerful.

clue.text: Regularly spying press in rough bars

indicators.note: taking letters at regular intervals means every other letter of the word

parts.note: to iron clothes is to press them

explanation.surface: Regular espionage on the press, ending up behind rough bars in prison.
explanation.definitionFit: Crude iron straight from the furnace is cast into ingots, rough bars of metal.

clue.text: Pair heartily keen to drop a complaint

indicators.note: the heart of a word is its middle letters
the single letter named is dropped from the other word

parts.note: to keen is to wail in grief, to lament

explanation.surface: A couple wholeheartedly eager to drop a grievance.
explanation.definitionFit: An illness, especially a minor one, is called a complaint.

clue.text: Metal guineas melted down in empty museum

indicators.note: one thing in another sits inside it
an emptied word keeps only its outside letters
melting coins down reshapes the metal, so these letters are reshaped

explanation.surface: Gold coins are melted down for their metal in a museum emptied of visitors.
explanation.walkthrough: A guinea was an old British gold coin, worth 21 shillings.
explanation.definitionFit: This light silvery element is one of the alkaline earth metals.

clue.text: Poor son reacted badly

indicators.note: something done badly is botched, so the letters come out in the wrong order

explanation.surface: A poor son reacted badly to something.
explanation.definitionFit: Second-rate means inferior in quality, which is what poor means here.

clue.text: Reportedly cause terrible smell

indicators.note: something reported is passed on by word of mouth, so the word is heard rather than read

parts.note: to wreak havoc is to cause it

explanation.surface: Something is said to cause a terrible smell.
explanation.definitionFit: A strong unpleasant stench is a reek.

clue.text: Water vole eviscerated bug

parts.note: pee is slang for urine, as in to pass water

indicators.note: to eviscerate is to gut, removing the insides and leaving the outer letters

explanation.surface: A water vole has been gutted, and a bug was responsible.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Water vole' looks like the animal; split it.
explanation.definitionFit: To bug someone is to irritate or annoy them, which is to peeve them.

clue.text: Closest friend follows professional team

indicators.note: one piece follows another, so it comes after it

parts.note: a pro is a professional
XI, eleven in Roman numerals, is a cricket or football team
a mate is a friend

explanation.surface: A close friend follows a professional sports team.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Closest friend' looks like one phrase; the definition is the first word alone.
explanation.definitionFit: Proximate means nearest or immediately adjacent, so closest.

clue.text: Nine pale security guards from Asia

indicators.note: the words guard the answer, holding it within them

explanation.surface: Nine pale-faced security guards have come from Asia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Security guards' reads as a job title; 'guards' is the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A person or thing from Nepal, a Himalayan country of Asia, is described this way.

clue.text: Bookmaker and boozer relish revels

parts.note: boozer is British slang for a pub

indicators.note: to revel is to make merry, so the letters run riot

explanation.surface: A bookie and a pub drinker enjoy revelling.
explanation.walkthrough: A bookmaker usually takes bets; here it is literal, a firm that makes books.
explanation.definitionFit: A firm that produces and issues books is literally a maker of books.

clue.text: Hollywood star cheers gagging order

indicators.note: a gag goes over the mouth, so one piece is held inside the other

parts.note: cheers is British for thank you, thanks
OM is the Order of Merit, a British honour

explanation.surface: A film star says thanks while a gagging order is imposed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gagging order' looks like a legal injunction; it is two jobs.
explanation.definitionFit: Tom Hanks is a leading American film actor, a Hollywood star.

clue.text: Husband eyeing dodgy sanitary practices

indicators.note: dodgy means unreliable, so the letters are not to be trusted in their order

explanation.surface: A husband warily eyeing unhygienic habits.
explanation.definitionFit: Practices of cleanliness that preserve health are what hygiene means.

clue.text: Squandered last of pension on cannabis

indicators.note: in an across clue one piece on another follows it

parts.note: blow is slang for cannabis

indicators.note: the last of a word is its final letter

explanation.surface: The last of the pension was squandered on cannabis.
explanation.definitionFit: To blow money is to waste it, so blown money has been squandered.

clue.text: Poem about matter initially incensing religious group

indicators.note: about means around, so the poem goes around the other piece

parts.note: an ode is a poem
pus is matter from a wound

indicators.note: initially means take the first letter

explanation.surface: A poem about some matter first incenses a religious group.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Matter' is not a topic but the discharge from a wound.
explanation.definitionFit: Opus Dei is a Catholic organisation, a religious group.

clue.text: Vivacity of Zulu monarch's beginning to go

parts.note: Zulu is Z in the NATO phonetic alphabet

indicators.note: the beginning of the word is to go, so its first letter is removed

parts.note: a king is a monarch

explanation.surface: A Zulu king's vigour starting to fade.
explanation.definitionFit: Zing is energy and liveliness, which is vivacity.

clue.text: Half-cut Pict slurs you cruelly and falsely

indicators.note: cruelly twisted, the letters are tormented into a new order
half cut off, so only the first half of the word is kept

explanation.surface: A drunk Pict slurs words cruelly and falsely at you.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Half-cut' is British slang for drunk; here it keeps PI, half of Pict. 'Cruelly' shuffles PI with SLURS YOU.
explanation.definitionFit: Spurious means false or not genuine, so the adverb means falsely.

clue.text: Guru perhaps crawled over island

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece over another sits above it

parts.note: the crawl is a swimming stroke, so to crawl is to swim

explanation.surface: A guru has crawled across an island.
explanation.definitionFit: A swami is a Hindu religious teacher, one kind of guru.

clue.text: Child leaves Loch Ness, ignoring new geological feature

indicators.note: to ignore something is to leave it out
the child leaves, so its letters are taken out

explanation.surface: A child walks away from Loch Ness, ignoring something new.
explanation.walkthrough: Loch Ness is a Scottish lake.
explanation.definitionFit: Loess is a fine windblown sediment deposit, a feature studied by geologists.

clue.text: Spooner's fish is allowed to do this when it's sunny

definitions.text: to do this when it's sunny

indicators.note: Spooner swapped the opening sounds of words, so the starts of the two pieces change places

parts.note: hake is a fish
may means is allowed

explanation.surface: A fish is permitted to do something when the sun is out.
explanation.walkthrough: The proverb says to make hay while the sun shines.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverb links haymaking to sunshine: seize the opportunity while conditions are good.

clue.text: Conservative kept dark study carpeted

parts.note: to keep something dark is to hide it, so hid
a den is a study, a private room for work

explanation.surface: A Conservative politician kept quiet about a study that has carpets.
explanation.definitionFit: To be carpeted is British slang for being scolded or reprimanded, as being chidden is.

clue.text: European with extremely macabre habit making you throw up

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its first and last letters

parts.note: a tic is a nervous habit

explanation.surface: A European with a ghoulish habit that turns your stomach.
explanation.definitionFit: An emetic substance induces vomiting.

clue.text: Privates from Ohio wreathed in smiles

indicators.note: something wreathed in another is wrapped round by it

parts.note: grins are broad smiles

explanation.surface: Soldiers from Ohio, all wreathed in smiles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Privates' looks like soldiers; it is the euphemism for the genital area.
explanation.definitionFit: The groin is the area of the genitals, euphemistically called one's privates.
